scope.membership: Active full members of Star Alliance, SkyTeam, and oneworld, plus documented current passenger airlines discovered in worldwide Wikipedia passenger, regional, and low-cost directories. Explicit affiliates retain their own membership type. Suspended members are distinguished from active members and independents. Alaska remains in oneworld.
scope.hubs: Wikipedia hubs, secondary hubs, operating bases, or focus cities; a directly documented operating-airport statement or directory hub cell can also establish an origin for small carriers. Headquarters cities and destination lists do not establish hubs. Roles and evidence are retained; no inferred all-to-all routes.
scope.routes: Passenger destination entries in each selected hub or base airport Wikipedia table, matched to the airline or explicitly enumerated service brands. Airport table entries are source-listed services, not independently verified nonstop flight schedules.
scope.seasonality: Seasonal services included and labeled; future and suspended/ended entries are separate. Undated listed entries reflect the retrieved page, not a guarantee of operation on as_of.
scope.coverage: Coverage status means the source table was parsed. It does not certify the source is exhaustive or up to date. See issues for every unresolved entry.
scope.direction: Records are hub-origin services. A route listed at both hubs appears in both directions; no reciprocal service is invented.

membership_notes: Alaska Airlines remains in oneworld and is not duplicated under Non-aligned.
For point-to-point airlines, explicitly identified major operating bases or focus cities are retained as their actual role rather than mislabeled as hubs.
LATAM, easyJet, Ryanair, and Wizz Air are represented as explicitly enumerated operating-brand groups where relevant; individual source service brands remain visible.

Selection is source-defined: Ryanair primary bases, Wizz Air largest bases, easyJet largest base, Vueling main/secondary bases; for carriers without such narrowing labels, all current infobox operating bases are included.
Condor Münster/Osnabrück base begins 2 November 2026, after snapshot, so is excluded as a current origin.
Alexandria is normalized to current IATA ALY (formerly HBE), effective 16 September 2026, using an explicit Aegean code-change bulletin; original Borg El Arab coordinates retained.

Worldwide directory discovery expands passenger, regional, and low-cost coverage; only origins with clean route evidence are admitted to the final snapshot. See the discovery audit for every candidate and exclusion.

discovery_audit.methodology: Three bounded worldwide inventories, not a claim to enumerate every airline. Redlinks, ceased/planned/cargo-only entries, unavailable airports, ambiguous identities, absent matching rows and rate-limited pages are explicitly retained. A mapped origin can have partial linked-destination coverage; those unresolved entries stay in dataset issues. Incidental operating-company links do not establish the marketing brand network.
